 This application coming on for admission this day, the
 following:
 Order

The first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending her arrest in connection with Crime No.76 of 2023 registered at Police Station Alampur, District Bhind (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
As per the case of prosecution, father of victim reported to PS Alampur, District Bhind that his daughter, aged around 17 years and 8 months, is missing since night of 24-09-2023.Some unknown person
has allured and taken his minor daughter.
On such allegations, PS Alampur, District Bhind registered FIR at Crime No.76 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC against unknown offender.
Victim was recovered from Chakla Gate, Outpost Metad, PS Gotad, (Gujarat) on 03-10-2023.
In her statement recorded under Section 161 of CrPC on 04-10-2023, victim stated that her uncle introduced her with one Sanjeeev Kushwah.
She used to converse with Sanjeev Kushwah on mobile phone.

On 22-09-2023, she called Sanjeev Kushwah and requested him to take along with Arti Ben vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141287317/
1 him otherwise she would die.

entities.text: Arti Ben vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 24-09-2023, her uncle brought some sleep pills.
She administered those sleep pills in food of family in the night.
Her uncle assisted her to reach Sanjeev Kushwah, who was waiting for her near the tower of Village.

Her uncle told them that she should go with Sanjeev Kushwah on motorcycle and they may marry in Court, therefore, she went with Sanjeev Kushwah to Alampur and from there, they boarded a four wheeler along with some other persons and went to Kota (Rajasthan).
Sanjeev Kushwah took her to Udaipur, but midway they deboarded bus and went to Tilakwada.
They stayed with paternal aunt of Sanjeev Kushwah for two days at there.
Applicant Arti Ben, happens to be daughter-in-law of paternal aunt of Sanjeev Kushwah, took them to her paternal home in Bota(Gujarat).
Her father, uncle and police team reached there and brought her to Alampur, District Bhind.
She further stated that Sanjeev Kushwah has allured and taken her to Badodra (Gujarat) for marring her, but he or any other persons have not committed any wrong act or misdemeanour with her.
Later in her statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, victim alleged rape against her uncle and indecent behaviour against Sanjeev Kushwah and his associates Pawan and Ajay.
There is no mention about the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC.
Accused Pawan, Sanjeev Kushwah, Raju alias Rajkumar, Lakhan Patwa and Ajay Kushwah were arrested.
Statements of witnesses have also been recorded.
Relevant seizure has been made.
Medico-legal examination of victim and accused has been conducted.
Later on, offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act was added.
Investigation is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the matter merely on the basis of statement of victim that she accompanied the victim and Sanjeev Kushwah to her matrimonial home in Village Bota in Gujarat.
The applicant was not aware about the minority of victim.
Further, she was not aware of the background of the incident.
She is a married woman with family comprising of two minor children.
She is a homemaker.
There is no likelihood of her absconsion leaving behind her family and home.
There is no likelihood of her tampering with evidence.
No custodial interrogation of applicant is required.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for State ably assisted by learned Counsel for complainant opposes anticipatory bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commencing on merits of the case, this Court inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.

C.C. as per rules.
